title: Towards ecologically meaningful foundation models
title_zh: 生态学基础模型的生态学意义之路
abstract: Ecology aims to explain and predict how organisms interact with each other and their environments across space and time. Yet both ecological data and theory are fragmented, leading to models that generalize poorly beyond specific systems or scales. Empirical evidence spans diverse modalities, resolutions and contexts, while theory is distributed across partially overlapping frameworks that are rarely integrated within a single predictive model. We argue that ecological foundation models (ecoFMs), trained on large, multi-modal ecological datasets and informed by ecological theory, offer a route towards unifying data and theory within a common framework. Beyond their scientific value for ecology, ecoFMs present a challenging and consequential testbed for machine learning, demanding advances in multi-modal representation learning, theory-guided modelling and uncertainty-aware inference. By learning shared representations of organisms, environments and interactions, ecoFMs could improve generalization, link pattern to process and enable synthesis across ecological subdisciplines. We outline a roadmap for developing ecoFMs, including requirements for data infrastructure, model architectures, evaluation strategies and governance, and assess where current machine learning and ecological approaches fall short. If developed responsibly and collaboratively with ecological practitioners and other actors, ecoFMs could enable new modes of analysis and strengthen ecological forecasting, while simultaneously driving advances in machine learning for multi-modal integration, theory-guided learning and generalization in complex, data-limited systems. Ecology struggles to make broad predictions, as ecological data and theories are scattered across many different sources, scales and approaches. Gardiner et al. propose to create ecological foundation models, which combine large, multi-modal ecological datasets with ecological theory, as a way to create more generalizable and predictive models.
abstract_zh: 生态学旨在解释和预测生物体在空间和时间中如何相互作用以及与环境的相互作用。然而，生态数据和理论都呈现出碎片化状态，导致模型在特定系统或尺度之外的泛化能力较差。实证证据涵盖多种模式、分辨率和情境，而理论则分布在部分重叠但很少在单一预测模型中整合的框架中。我们认为，生态基础模型（ecoFMs）通过在大规模、多模态生态数据上训练并结合生态理论，提供了一条统一数据与理论的途径。除了在生态学方面的科学价值外，ecoFMs 还是机器学习具有挑战性且后果重大的试验场，要求在多模态表征学习、基于理论的建模和不确定性感知推断方面取得进步。通过学习生物体、环境和相互作用的共同表示，ecoFMs 可以提高泛化能力，将模式与过程联系起来，并跨生态学亚学科实现综合。我们概述了开发 ecoFMs 的路线图，包括数据基础设施、模型结构、评估策略和治理的要求，并评估当前机器学习和生态学方法的不足。如果负责任且与生态实践者及其他利益相关者合作开发，ecoFMs 可以实现新的分析模式，加强生态预测，同时推动多模态整合、基于理论学习以及在数据有限系统中泛化的机器学习进步。生态学难以进行广泛预测，因为生态数据和理论分散在许多不同的来源、尺度和方法中。Gardiner 等人提议创建生态基础模型，通过结合大规模、多模态生态数据与生态理论，以创建更具普适性和可预测性的模型。
